findings.title: The DEAD-scan refusal gained a conjunct: a scan whose population counter reads zero no longer stops the run when it happens to have hits
findings.before: `if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` (both loops of `Scan.report`) and `r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && println(io, "prepare: DEAD scan $(r.id) — $(r.note)")`
findings.after: `if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)` (both loops) and `(r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)) && println(io, "prepare: DEAD scan $(r.id) — $(r.note)")`
findings.why_it_matters: Concrete input that used to be refused and is now accepted: a `ScanResult` with `population == 0`, `exempted == 0` and a non-empty `hits`. SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE can produce exactly this — `return (hits, length(units))` where `units = prose_units(cfg)` is the FIRST loop's enumeration while the SECOND loop pushes `# Fields`/`!!!`-ordering hits from `docstring_blocks` independently of it (src/Scans/prose_shape.jl:98,115-126,128). If `prose_units` stops enumerating (the exact 'a parser that stops matching' failure the package builds `min_types` into `display_gate` to catch), the old code printed `DEAD SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE measured nothing` and returned 2 — `gbg scan docs` and `gbg round prepare` both refused. The new code prints `FAIL` with the two surviving hits and returns 1, and the fact that the ratchet measured no unit at all is never printed anywhere. Exit 2 (cannot evaluate) has silently become exit 1 (finding) for a whole class, and CLAUDE.md makes exit codes the contract. The `ScanResult` docstring at head still says the opposite and was NOT touched by this diff: '`population` — what the scan measured …; zero means the scan measured nothing and is DEAD' (src/Scan.jl:36-37).
findings.description: The comment added with the change — 'a scan that HIT measured something: its hits are never dropped by the dead branch' — names a REPORTING defect (the DEAD branch printed no hits) and fixes it by deleting the DEAD verdict instead. The narrow fix is to print the hits and still mark DEAD with code 2. As written the edit is wider than the defect twice over: it removes the refusal rather than the silence, and it removes it in three places at once including `prepare`'s independent warning. It is also redundant with the same commit's own narrower fix — `src/Scans/field_docs.jl` was separately re-counted so its NOLIST hits no longer land with population 0 — so the concrete case that motivated the change was already handled at its source.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `src/Scan.jl @@ -435,16 +436,21 @@`: `-        if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` / `+        # a scan that HIT measured something: its hits are never dropped by the dead branch` / `+        if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)`. Unchanged at head, src/Scan.jl:36: '- `population` — what the scan measured (files, docstrings, exports, arguments or pages); zero means the scan measured nothing and is DEAD.'

findings.title: SCAN.FIELD_DOCS now counts structs it could say nothing about, defeating the vacuous-pass guard its own header still describes
locations: src/Scans/field_docs.jl:4-5 (the header sentence left in place)
findings.before: `if documented === nothing` / `    isempty(real) || push!(hits, Hit(f, line, "NOLIST …"; symbol = name))` / `    continue` / `end` / `checked += 1`
findings.after: `checked += 1                                          # every struct opened was checked: a` / `if documented === nothing                                 # NOLIST hit with population 0 reads as a DEAD scan` / `    isempty(real) || push!(hits, Hit(f, line, "NOLIST …"; symbol = name))` / `    continue` / `end`
findings.why_it_matters: `checked` is the scan's `population`, and population 0 is the DEAD/exit-2 refusal. Concrete input that used to be refused: a consumer whose structs declare fields without type annotations (`struct Point x; y end`) or whose docstrings do not use the literal marker `The fields are`. `documented_fields` returns `nothing` for every struct and `real_fields` (`FIELD_DECL = r"^\s{2,}([^\s:=#]+)\s*::"`, src/Scans/field_docs.jl:8) returns empty, so no NOLIST fires. Before: `checked == 0` → `DEAD SCAN.FIELD_DOCS measured nothing`, exit 2 — correct, because the scan verified nothing. After: `checked == N`, zero hits, and the report prints `ok SCAN.FIELD_DOCS (N)` — a clean bill for a corpus in which the scan compared no field against any bullet. The failure it was built to catch is a marker or `FIELD_DECL` reword by a refactor, which now passes vacuously in exactly the way the file's own header forbids.
findings.description: The defect being fixed (a NOLIST-only run reading as DEAD) is real, but the fix redefines the scan's population from 'structs whose bullets were compared' to 'structs opened', which is not what population means anywhere else in `Scan.jl` ('what the scan measured'). A fix that preserves the guard is to count a struct as measured when EITHER a documented list or a real field list was successfully parsed — that admits the NOLIST run and still reports DEAD when both parsers come back empty. The header comment stating the old contract was left verbatim, so the file now documents a guard its code no longer has.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `src/Scans/field_docs.jl @@ -47,11 +47,11 @@`: `-            if documented === nothing` … `-            checked += 1` / `+            checked += 1                                          # every struct opened was checked: a` / `+            if documented === nothing                                 # NOLIST hit with population 0 reads as a DEAD scan`. Untouched at head, src/Scans/field_docs.jl:4-5: 'Zero documented structs ⇒ population 0 (DEAD): a parser broken by a refactor fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.'

findings.title: SCAN.MATHBF hardcodes `\mathbf{1}` into the allowed set, making `notation.mathbf_allowed` partly inert and this package's own empty list a lie
locations: src/Scans/mathbf.jl:1-4 (the header rewritten in the same commit)
policy/latex-idiom.md:59-60 (the rule paragraph amended in the same commit)
findings.before: `allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"]))` — and the header: '# `notation.mathbf_allowed` (PF admits `\mathbf{1}`; a package on `notation.vectors = "boldsymbol"` lists nothing more).'
findings.after: `allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}")` — and the header: '`\mathbf{1}` … is admitted in every package whatever that list holds, so it is never a hit.'
findings.why_it_matters: Concrete input that used to be refused: any `\mathbf{1}` in a package whose config omits it from `notation.mathbf_allowed`. This is not hypothetical — the tool's OWN `.gbg/config.toml:67` reads `mathbf_allowed = []`, the deliberate empty list the base header describes for a `boldsymbol`/no-vector package. Before this commit a `\mathbf{1}` written into any docstring or rationale page of GBGCodingTools was a hard hit and failed the scan; after it, no consumer can make the scan report it, and the config key no longer determines what the scan admits. The register still states the opposite: `policy/RULES.toml:357` `statement = "\\mathbf is admitted only for the strings in notation.mathbf_allowed; vectors follow notation.vectors."` and its sentinel '`\mathbf` is admitted only for an agreed list of strings…' — both unchanged by this diff, as is the §12.A row that quotes the statement.
findings.description: This is the shape the audit brief names: a guard removed from the code and, in the same commit, the prose that stated the guard rewritten to legitimise the removal — `policy/latex-idiom.md` gained 'it is not a package's to withhold' while `RULES.toml`'s one-line statement and sentinel, which are the register the instruments cite and `LEG.SENTINELS` reads, still say the config list is the sole authority. The stated motive (RULE.TEX.MATHBB names `\mathbf{1}` as the indicator) argues for adding `\mathbf{1}` to the SCHEMA DEFAULT — which already carries it (`schema/config.schema.json:304-309`) — not for overriding a package that explicitly cleared the list. As it stands the tool's own config says one thing and the scan does another, with no ledger entry recording the deviation.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `src/Scans/mathbf.jl @@ -1,8 +1,9 @@`: `-    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"]))` / `+    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}")`. Diff hunk `policy/latex-idiom.md @@ -56,7 +56,8 @@`: `-outside the admitted list.` / `+outside the admitted list. `\mathbf{1}`, the indicator and identity of `RULE.TEX.MATHBB`, is admitted in` / `+every package whatever that list holds; it is not a package's to withhold.`. `.gbg/config.toml:67: mathbf_allowed = []`.

findings.title: The latex-typesetter hat lost its `rulebook` need, so it is no longer handed the rulebook its persona orders it to read first
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/panel.js:87 (the line that is now never emitted for this hat)
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:230-231 (`not_applicable`, which this hat can no longer reach)
findings.after: `needs = ["source"]              # the persona reads the rendered policy file, never a `rulebook_sections` grant`
findings.why_it_matters: `panel.js` emits the rulebook only under that need: `if (needs.includes('rulebook')) parts.push(`THE RULEBOOK (AUTHORITATIVE — read it first, in full): ${A.rulebook_path}`)`. `A.rulebook_path` is `payload/rulebook.md`, and `Preflight.rulebook_text` (src/CLI/Preflight.jl:330-341) builds it from the RENDERED POLICY FILES first and the `rulebook_sections` afterwards — so the rendered `latex-idiom.md` reaches this hat through that grant and through nothing else. The unchanged persona still opens 'Your rubric is NOT generic taste — FIRST read the house rulebook named in your substrate (the rendered policy file `latex-idiom.md`, with the package's notation parameters substituted into it) and treat it as AUTHORITATIVE.' After this edit the substrate names no such file: the hat that enforces the house LaTeX idiom now judges on generic taste, in the tool's own roster and the fixture's (`.gbg/config.toml:127`, `fixture/GBG Fixture/.gbg/config.toml:89` both list `latex-typesetter`). Second loss: `na = … || ("rulebook" in needs && isempty(cfg["package"]["rulebook_sections"]))` — this hat can no longer be marked `not_applicable`, so in a consumer with no rulebook sections it now runs and reports as a live lane instead of being marked and not expected.
findings.description: The comment justifies the removal by claiming the persona reads the rendered policy file rather than a `rulebook_sections` grant, but the rendered policy file is delivered BY that grant — `rulebook_text` writes the policy files and the sections into one payload, and `needs = ["rulebook"]` is the only switch that puts its path in the prompt. `catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml` kept `needs = ["rulebook", "source"]` for the same reason, so the two rulebook hats are now inconsistent. Either the persona's first sentence should have been rewritten with the need, or the need should have stayed; removing one half leaves a dead pointer in an instrument that is frozen mid-round.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `catalog/hats/latex-typesetter.toml @@ -1,7 +1,7 @@`: `-needs = ["source", "rulebook"]` / `+needs = ["source"]              # the persona reads the rendered policy file, never a `rulebook_sections` grant`; the persona line below it is unchanged: 'FIRST read the house rulebook named in your substrate (the rendered policy file `latex-idiom.md` …) and treat it as AUTHORITATIVE.'

findings.title: The requirement that `docs_build` name `docs/make.jl` was deleted from the specification instead of being implemented
findings.before: ARCHITECTURE §7.3: '`docs_build` names `docs/make.jl` and that file exists'; the config example: '# CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl'; `check_paths`: 'the `docs/make.jl` that `docs_build` names'.
findings.after: ARCHITECTURE §7.3: 'the fixed path `docs/make.jl` a consumer's `docs_build` is expected to run exists'; the config example: '# CFG.SURFACES requires docs/make.jl to exist'; `check_paths`: 'the fixed path `docs/make.jl` a consumer's `docs_build` command is expected to run'.
findings.why_it_matters: `src/CLI/Config.jl:208` is `isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, …)` and is unchanged by this diff — the check never read `docs_build` at all. Rather than build the missing half, the commit rewrote the design record and the docstring so the weaker behaviour is what is specified. Concrete input a consumer can now set and have every check pass: `docs_build = "julia --project=docs other/build.jl"`, or `docs_build = "true"`. Nothing else closes the hole — `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` (src/CLI/Doctor.jl:376-384) inspects the CONTENTS of `docs/make.jl` and never the configured command, and `docs_build` is otherwise only executed (`Rounds.build`, `Rounds.prepare`, `Passes`, `BUILD.DOCS`). The tool's whole docs-side assurance — the `makedocs` wrapper runs the quick doctor, the hard scans and the closure gate — rests on the configured build command actually reaching the wrapper, which is now nowhere verified and, after this edit, nowhere required either.
findings.description: Correcting a docstring that overstated a check is right; deleting the requirement from the DESIGN RECORD in the same edit is not the same act, and it leaves no trace that a stated refusal was dropped. The commit that introduces `RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK`'s `check` field — whose whole point is that a rule without a check is a declared weakness rather than a silent one — resolves this gap in the opposite direction, by removing the rule. The honest forms were to keep the §7.3 wording and add the two-line check to `check_paths`, or to keep it and record the gap.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md @@ -1735,7 +1743,7 @@`: `-| `CFG.SURFACES` | … `docs_build` names `docs/make.jl` and that file exists; …` / `+| `CFG.SURFACES` | … the fixed path `docs/make.jl` a consumer's `docs_build` is expected to run exists; …`. Diff hunk `@@ -1113,7 +1120,7 @@`: `-docs_build  = "julia --project=docs docs/make.jl"            # CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl` / `+…# CFG.SURFACES requires docs/make.jl to exist`. `src/CLI/Config.jl` shows no code change in this diff.

findings.title: RULE.DOC.SHAPE is registered as mechanically checked in the same commit that records the check does not enforce it on baselined page units
findings.before: Scan header: 'Caps bind ALWAYS (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions; IT's lesson: a cap that applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming).' §12.B: 'caps 120 words / 3 admonitions always'.
findings.after: Scan header: 'Caps … bind on every docstring and every NEW page unit; a page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone, the one place IT's lesson … is traded for an append-only log.' §12.B: 'caps 120 words / 3 admonitions on every docstring and every NEW page unit, a baselined page unit held by the ratchet alone'.
findings.why_it_matters: The scan's code (`if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing`) is unchanged, so no behaviour moved — what moved is the STATED norm, in the loosening direction, in two places. Meanwhile the rule the scan claims to enforce was not loosened: `policy/docs-rubric.md`'s RULE.DOC.SHAPE paragraph is untouched by this diff and `policy/RULES.toml`'s statement still reads 'A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always'. The same commit then stamps that rule `check = ["scan:SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE"]`, which the new `RULES.toml` header defines as 'what catches the rule's next violation'. A baselined page section that today sits at 300 words is a standing violation of the rule as written that the named check will never report, and the register now certifies it as caught. `weakness` — the class this commit created precisely for 'a check is possible and none is built' — would have recorded the gap instead of closing it on paper.
findings.description: Two of the three documents describing this cap were relaxed to match the code and the third, the rule itself, was left strict; the new `check` field then asserts the relaxed check enforces the strict rule. Either the rule paragraph should have been relaxed with them (a policy change, with its own ledger consequences) or the `check` entry should have carried a recorded partiality. The new test in `test/schemas.jl` cannot tell the difference: it only asserts the scan id exists in the catalogue.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `src/Scans/prose_shape.jl @@ -1,8 +1,9 @@`: `-# item `NN. ` … Caps bind` / `-# ALWAYS (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions; IT's lesson: …)` / `+# Caps` / `+# (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions) bind on every docstring and every NEW page unit; a` / `+# page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone`. `policy/RULES.toml` head, unchanged statement: 'A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always'.

findings.title: The new rule-check oracle verifies a `harness:` binding by bare substring — the exact match the same file's other test was narrowed to reject
locations: test/schemas.jl:96-97 (the sibling test narrowed in the same commit)
findings.before: No such test existed; `RULES.toml` carried no `check` field.
findings.after: `elseif startswith(c, "harness:")` / `    @test occursin(last(split(c[9:end], '.')) * "(", srctext)` — where `srctext` is every `.jl` file under `src/` concatenated.
findings.why_it_matters: Eleven rules resolve their entire enforcement claim through this arm — `RULE.INST.NO_TRUNCATION` → `harness:report`, `RULE.DOC.BUILD_VERIFY` and `RULE.TEST.EXAMPLES_RUN` → `harness:makedocs`, `RULE.DOC.BATTERY` → `harness:Preflight.resolve_checkdocs_lanes`, four more on `TestHarness.*`, three on `Passes.grade`/`Witnesses.run`/`Preflight.render_args`. The assertion is satisfied by the literal `report(` occurring anywhere in `src/**.jl`, including inside a comment, a docstring or an unrelated call. Nine lines earlier in the same file, the same commit removed a disjunct for exactly this reason, with the reason written out: 'the name must appear on a line that LOADS a schema, never merely somewhere in the source: `finding` matched a coincidental substring and the schema was validated against nothing'. The new arm reproduces the shape the commit had just diagnosed, so the oracle guarding the diff's headline mechanism — every rule names its enforcer — is weaker than the one it sits beside.
findings.description: All eleven `harness:` targets happen to resolve to real bindings today, so nothing is currently mis-certified; the concern is the guard, not the present state. A rename or deletion of `Passes.grade`, `Witnesses.run` or `Preflight.render_args` leaves three rules claiming an enforcer that no longer exists and this test green, because some other `grade(`/`run(`/`render_args(` survives in 60-odd source files. The narrowing the sibling test received — require the token on a line that also carries the defining construct — applies here unchanged.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `test/schemas.jl @@ -126,4 +143,28 @@`: `+                elseif startswith(c, "harness:")` / `+                    @test occursin(last(split(c[9:end], '.')) * "(", srctext)`. Diff hunk `@@ -93,9 +93,26 @@` in the same file: `-            @test occursin("load_schema(\"" * name * "\")", src) || occursin("\"" * name * "\"", src)` / `+            # the name must appear on a line that LOADS a schema, never merely somewhere in the source:` / `+            # `finding` matched a coincidental substring and the schema was validated against nothing`.

findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM's type exemption was widened from a literal to a whitespace-tolerant regex, skipping docstrings it previously judged
findings.before: `occursin("The fields are:", d.body) && continue               # a type documents fields (RULE.DOC.FIELDS)` and `const ARGS_BULLET = "The arguments are:"`
findings.after: `occursin(r"The\s+fields\s+are:", d.body) && continue          # a type documents fields (RULE.DOC.FIELDS)` and `const ARGS_BULLET = r"The\s+arguments\s+are:"`
findings.why_it_matters: The `continue` is a whole-docstring exemption from SCAN.ARGS_FORM, and `\s` includes the newline, so a docstring whose text wraps as 'The fields\nare:' — or one that merely writes 'The  fields are:' — is now skipped where before it was judged and could hit `wrong-args-form`. The same widening on `ARGS_BULLET` is mixed rather than one-directional: a wrapped marker now counts as bulleted, which suppresses the `wants_bullets && !bulleted` hit (the direction the comment gives as the motive) but also newly fires the `!wants_bullets && bulleted` and the mixed-forms hits. The population is unaffected either way, so the loosening is invisible to the DEAD detector.
findings.description: The motive stated in the added comment — 'the marker line-wraps in this package's own prose, and a literal substring missed it' — is a real false negative and the regex is the right shape for the two argument markers. The fields exemption is the collateral: it was not the false negative being fixed, and widening a whole-docstring skip is the one edit in this file that removes hits rather than adding them. Recorded at nit because the surface is small and the same commit's other edits to this scan (balanced-paren signature parsing, splat counting) move it firmly in the strict direction.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `src/Scans/args_form.jl @@ -3,19 +3,44 @@`: `-const ARGS_BULLET = "The arguments are:"` / `+# whitespace-tolerant: the marker line-wraps in this package's own prose, and a literal substring missed it` / `+const ARGS_BULLET = r"The\s+arguments\s+are:"`, and `-        occursin("The fields are:", d.body) && continue               # a type documents fields (RULE.DOC.FIELDS)` / `+        occursin(r"The\s+fields\s+are:", d.body) && continue          # a type documents fields (RULE.DOC.FIELDS)`.
